intended_use: Preliminary marine fuel storage and payload screening. Not a ship design, tank certification, or route-specific bunkering model.
comparison_policy: Separate fuel-only LHV from tank-included system energy density.
Do not treat MGO/MDO/HFO as interchangeable fuel labels.
Tank-included values depend on the study's tank type, pressure, temperature, insulation and containment assumptions.
Do not add the tank penalty twice when using a tank-included value.
These values do not include all ship structure, engine, fuel conditioning, ventilation, fire suppression, piping, bunkering, reserve or safety-system mass/volume unless the source explicitly says so.
Fuel pathway lifecycle emissions are independent of volumetric and gravimetric energy density; high energy density does not mean low lifecycle GHG.

design_implications: A ship fuel comparison must account for tank-system energy density and usable storage volume before claiming equal range or payload.
The same engine efficiency does not imply the same vessel range, cargo capacity or bunker frequency.
For long-distance ships, report tank volume, tank mass, fuel mass, usable energy, endurance, payload displacement and bunkering logistics together.
For coastal and inland cargo, route-specific bunkering frequency may be a better trade-off than maximizing stored energy.
A fuel-flexible engine cannot compensate for a storage system that removes too much revenue cargo or requires impractical cryogenic / pressure infrastructure.
